missing.name: OMP_NUM_THREADS

readers.program: GNUmakefile (make, while it parses the file), through the nproc command of GNU coreutils
readers.mechanism: $(shell nproc ...): the nproc program reads the variable. No line of the checkout names it

missing.values: A positive integer. nproc prints this number in place of the CPU count. Measured: 3 gave 3, 1 gave 1, and 40 gave 40 on a host where plain nproc printed 6. For a comma-separated list nproc used the first number (4,2 gave 4). The values 0, -1, abc and empty text were ignored (nproc printed 6).
missing.default: Unset: nproc prints the number of CPUs that the process may use. The variable is not read at all when NPROC_BUILD is already defined, because line 96 is inside ifndef NPROC_BUILD (GNUmakefile:95).
missing.effect: It changes the default of NPROC_BUILD, which is the smaller of 16 and the nproc output (GNUmakefile:96). NPROC_BUILD is the job count that the makefile adds to MAKEFLAGS (GNUmakefile:209) and passes to every cmake --build (for example GNUmakefile:404). A value of 1 gives a serial build. A value above 16 has no effect because of the cap.
missing.notes: The fact that nproc reads this variable is a measurement, not a statement of the checkout. Measured on 2026-11-22 with nproc of GNU coreutils 8.32. OMP_THREAD_LIMIT is read by the same nproc call and has an entry (area shell-rest). OMP_NUM_THREADS=40 with OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=4 gave 4, so the limit has priority. The shell-rest verifier rejected OMP_NUM_THREADS because no line of the checkout names it, and recorded the same measurement in the notes of OMP_THREAD_LIMIT. It is listed here because a person can have OMP_NUM_THREADS exported in the shell, and the build job count then changes with no message. GNUmakefile:96 is the only nproc call in the checkout.

missing.values: File path text. make expands a value from the environment as make syntax, so make functions in the value run.
missing.default: The makefile assigns gen/.fuse_stats_stamp at line 357 for every goal set that has a goal other than list-tests and list-tests-core. A value in the environment is then ignored. When the only goals are list-tests or list-tests-core, the makefile does not assign the name. A value from the environment is then used. Unset there means empty text.
missing.effect: Only when the only goals are list-tests or list-tests-core: make puts the environment value into the prerequisite lists of gen-deb/<package file>, gen/config/core, gen/config/dev, gen/config/test and gen/config/prod while it parses. make does not build those targets for these goals, so a plain path changes no result. A value with make functions, for example $(shell ...), runs those functions during parsing.
missing.notes: This is an internal make variable, not a documented setting. It is listed because the environment can supply it on the one path where the makefile does not assign it. HAS_AVX512 and TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED have entries for the same reason. list-tests and list-tests-core have no prerequisites (GNUmakefile:1143-1147). Checked with GNU Make 4.3 on a stand-alone copy of the construct outside the checkout: with the goal list-tests the origin of the variable was environment, the value appeared in the prerequisite list, and a $(shell ...) value ran at parse time. With another goal the origin was file. The repository makefile itself was not run. Lowest priority for the document.

same removal for the probe that runs with IN_NIX_SHELL=1
same removal for the probe that runs with CI=1
same removal for the probe of the deb goal

missing.values: Not applicable. The script only removes the name and never gives it a value.
missing.default: No file of the checkout reads the name or gives it a value.

missing.notes: MFLAGS is a GNU make variable. Whether GNU make takes MFLAGS from the environment: not determined: the checkout does not say, and it was not measured. The same four commands also remove MAKEFLAGS, MAKELEVEL and MAKECMDGOALS, which have entries. The comment on line 4 of the script gives a reason only for MAKECMDGOALS. The shell-ci verifier rejected MFLAGS because it is only removed. Other areas list names that are only removed, for example COVERAGE_PROCESS_START and PYTHONIOENCODING (python-rest) and PYTHONHOME (python-bin). It is listed here to keep one rule. Low priority for the document.

rejected_groups.reason: CMake variable. Every use is ${NAME} in CMake code (CMakeLists.txt, *.cmake) or in CMake text that a test script or a Python test writes. It is never $ENV{NAME}. Includes CMake cache variables and compile definitions such as SCRATCH_DIR.

Shell variable that the same script assigns before every use and does not export. Includes names that come from a sourced file of the checkout (perfetto/launcher-common), from /etc/os-release (ID, VERSION_ID) and from a coproc (PERFETTO_CLIENT). No default form ${NAME:-...} on the name itself.
Variable that bash maintains itself. A value from the caller is not used.
Shell local of one workflow step, one lefthook command or one makefile recipe. The step assigns it before use and does not export it.
Make variable that the makefile assigns itself with := on every path, or a make built-in (CURDIR). The environment cannot supply it.

Python module constant, standard library attribute or local name on a line that also has the text env. It is not an environment name. Constants that hold an environment name hold a name that the inventory already has, for example DICE_GRANT_ID_ENV = DICE_GRANT_ID and HARMONY_VOCAB_DIR_ENV = TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE.
C, C++ or Rust macro or constant, Catch2 macro, CMake keyword or value, or Haskell constructor.
Ordinary word, abbreviation or placeholder in a comment, a message, a help text or a test title.
Name prefix, not a full name. The code uses it to remove or to describe a family of names. The verified inventory records these places under dynamic_sites.

Named in the checkout but not read and not set as an environment variable: a comment example, a misspelled name in a comment (POS_NR_HUGEPAGE), the name of another product (VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE), a commented-out line (TORCH_LOGS), a C library constant (LC_TIME), the $ORIGIN token of the dynamic loader, a secret input name of a shared workflow (SSH_PRIVATE_KEY), unit-test data (SECRET), or an assertion that the name is absent (TRON_PROXY_VOCAB_SIZE).

Lower-case or mixed-case $name. Shell locals (assignment, read, for, local, function arguments), CMake variables, Nix values and Nix builder variables ($out, $src), jq, awk and sed text, and skill names in prompts. The 23 lower-case names that a shell script expands without an assignment were opened one by one. Each was a read-loop variable, a variable of a sourced file, or text of another language inside a string.

NAME=value text that is not an environment assignment: make command-line variables (DEB_NAME, CMAKELISTS, HEADERS, SOURCES, DOCS, SHELL), CMake -D options and compile definitions (BUILD_INGEST_MODELS, RINZLER_BINARY_PATH, TRON_*_ENABLED), HTML attributes in Graphviz labels, log and comment text, and shell locals (IFS, CUTOFF_EPOCH). Found by a sweep of every NAME= token in the tree.

Named only in a comment, and a third-party tool reads it: FORCE_COLOR at t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py:2600-2603. The comment says that pytest in the nested run honours it and that PY_COLORS=0 (line 2604) has priority. TRON code does not read it and does not set it. See disagreements.

Python upper-case string constant that is not an environment name: argparse metavar, attribute name for monkeypatch.setattr, status word, column title of LSF output, ctest property name, CMake variable name in generated text.

C, C++, Rust or Haskell upper-case string literal that is not an environment name: test data, enum text, log tag, option metavar, grammar terminal. Every literal passed to getenv, setenv, putenv or unsetenv (85 names) is already in the inventory.
Lower-case text that the Python environment-context extractor matched but that is a value or a key of another map, not a name (for example the IN_NIX_SHELL values pure and impure).

Token that shares a prefix with a well-known variable family (FUSE_, PERFETTO_, MAKE_, HF_, NIX_, LSF_, RUST_, PYTHON_ and others) but is a C macro, a C++ or Python constant, a CMake variable or a make variable. Found by a filter over all 3,749 upper-case tokens of the tree that are not in the inventory.

Make variable with only conditional assignments that the environment still cannot supply in effect. Both branches assign it (STDERR_FILTER, IOTOOLS_DEBUG), or every reference is inside the same conditional block (SCRATCH_DRY_FLAGS, TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_INDEPENDENT_GOALS, TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_UPDATE), or the only reference is in a recipe that cannot run on the path without the assignment (SCRATCH_DIRS, used only by distclean), or the assignment is recursive and comes before any expansion (DEFS).

notes: Scope of the sweep. git ls-files lists 1,420 tracked files. 120 Markdown files were left out by the task. 54 files were skipped: 46 binary files (41 png, 3 parquet, 1 pdf, 1 safetensors), the two prebuilt programs bin/yq and bin/iotools-1.5/iotools, 5 symbolic links under .claude/skills (their targets under .agents/skills were scanned) and the dangling link compile_commands.json. 1,246 text files were scanned. Step 1 result. 2,072 distinct names sit on a line with an environment cue. 472 are in the inventory. 608 upper-case names and 992 lower-case or mixed-case names were left. All 1,600 were triaged, and none is a missing variable. Blind spot of step 1. 53 of the 525 inventory names have no cue line (multi-line Python dictionaries, make variables, Nix attributes, workflow env keys, names read inside libraries). So ten more extractors were run: every getenv, setenv, putenv, unsetenv, environ call in C, C++ and Rust; the Python syntax tree of 241 Python files (237 names in environment contexts, 77 accesses with a non-constant key, all resolved); every env key, env., vars., secrets. expression and run block of the 13 workflows and lefthook.yml (103 names); the four makefiles; the 21 Nix files (133 names); $ENV{}, find ENV, cmake -E env, ENVIRONMENT properties and CMakePresets.json; the systemd units; every NAME= token; every upper-case string literal; and every name removed with env -u or unset. These extractors gave 450 further candidate names. candidates_checked = 2051: 2,050 distinct candidate names from all sweeps plus OMP_NUM_THREADS, which no file names. Main result. No variable that TRON product code reads is missing. Every literal name in a getenv-family call of C, C++ and Rust, every name in a Python environment access, every workflow, CMake, Nix and systemd name is in the inventory. The four entries under missing are marginal. OMP_NUM_THREADS is the only one that a person can meet in practice. FUSE_STATS_STAMP and PRESET_STAMP are internal make variables that the environment can supply only for the goals list-tests and list-tests-core. MFLAGS is only removed by one CI test. Inclusion rule that the document authors must decide. The verified inventory is not uniform on three points. (1) Names that only a tool reads: OMP_THREAD_LIMIT, LNAME, USERNAME, GHCRTS and the proxy names have entries, OMP_NUM_THREADS, FORCE_COLOR, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR and TEMPDIR do not. (2) Names that are only removed: python-rest and python-bin list them, shell-ci rejected MFLAGS. (3) Internal make variables that the environment can supply on some path: HAS_AVX512, TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED, CMAKE_DEFINES and IOTOOLS_STATIC have entries, FUSE_STATS_STAMP and PRESET_STAMP were not looked at. Reader sites that existing entries may lack. curl runs at bin/ci/ci-install-fourmolu.sh:20, bin/ci/setup-ghc.sh:40, rust/rust-toolchain.sh:221 and perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:290. The proxy entries (http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy and the upper-case forms) list only Python readers. That curl reads these names is not stated in the checkout and was not measured here. Stale source comments found during triage (not Markdown): src/system/huge.cpp:65-71 names POS_NR_HUGEPAGE, but the code reads POS_NR_HUGEPAGES (src/pos/driver.cpp:272). t/testutil.cpp:105-106 prints $SCRATCH_DIR, but SCRATCH_DIR is a compile-time definition from the CMake cache (CMakeLists.txt:60, t/CMakeLists.txt:50). bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:56 says $SUDO_USER, but the code uses $SUDO_UID (line 177). What was run. Only read commands on the checkout. Two things ran outside the checkout: the nproc program of the agent host with OMP_NUM_THREADS and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT set, and GNU Make 4.3 on a four-rule makefile in the scratch directory that copies the conditional of GNUmakefile:266-363. No repository script, makefile or test was run. Not covered. Markdown files, generated code under gen/ and build/ (absent), the inside of the two prebuilt programs, and variables that a third-party tool reads when no line of the checkout names them, except OMP_NUM_THREADS.
